why: Every edit is named, but commits 2 and 4 rewrite what reaches the server's and the browser's text registry (lazy makers, a setTimeout chain, a stamp poll, a used flag written during render), and the main proof of commit 4 is a mock-driven unit test the cheap model writes itself, answering by SQL text, which it can bend until it passes. The e2e suite only draws hand-written languages, so English words or stale text on an AI-translated store, or a poll that never stops or never runs, would pass every check; commit 3 is a generated migration, which wants a look before CI applies it.
harm_if_wrong: A store in an AI-translated language serves English or stale interface text (or a hydration mismatch) on every instance, or instances poll the database far more than planned, with no failing check.
make_it_cheaper: Write the body of src/server/ui-text-read.test.ts (the mocked readDb answers and the seven cases) into the brief verbatim, and add an e2e or int case that renders a seeded AI-translated store page and asserts a translated label, so commit 4 has a check the cheap model cannot shape.
brief_problems: docs/audits/bloat-review-2026-11/scripts/import-reach.mjs does not exist yet (step 0.1 makes it); commits 1 and 4 cannot run that check until 0.1 has landed.

refresh() and poll() read the stamp from the one platform_settings row: if that row is missing (a test database that never seeded it) the statement returns no row and the reader forgets every language, and bumpUiVersion's update silently does nothing; the brief does not say to treat no row as stamp 0.
Commit 2's 'registerMessages(lang, { …, texts: <the returns record> })' leaves the '…' to be read as the ui and email values loadLanguage already registers.

The 'under 150 statements a day' case sits close to its bound (144 ticks plus 2 at start); a second poll path through ensureUi() would push it over, and the brief does not say ensureUi() is not called in that case.
